PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Rerun Offline Inspector Entity Tree V2

## Summary
Refactor the offline inspector around a semantic Rerun tree: ASE observations under `world/ase`, GT supervision under `world/gt`, candidate pose diagnostics under `world/candidates`, EFM evidence under `world/efm`, and plots under `plots`. Replace aggregate manual candidate `LineStrips3D` frusta with native Rerun camera entities, log all candidates once under valid/invalid status, and attach expensive modalities only to one selected candidate.

The old manual line strips were used because one aggregate entity could carry all candidate frusta, colors, and labels. With native Rerun camera frusta, each candidate needs its own `Transform3D + Pinhole` camera entity; that is the cleaner contract now.

## Key Changes
- Entity tree:
  - `world/ase/semidense`, `world/ase/reference/rig`, `world/ase/trajectory/rig`
  - `world/ase/cameras/rgb/frame_{first,last}/camera/{image,depth}`
  - `world/gt/mesh`, `world/gt/obbs`
  - `world/efm/obbs/detected`, `world/efm/voxels/{occ_pr,cent_pr,cent_pr_nms}`
  - `world/candidates/{valid,invalid}/candidate_XXX/camera`
  - `world/candidates/{valid,invalid}/candidate_XXX/{depth,points,center}` only for the selected detail candidate where applicable
  - `metadata/candidates/table`, `metadata/sample`, and `plots/candidates/rri_histogram`

- Candidate logging:
  - Default native camera/frustum logging mode is `all`, grouped once by validity: `valid` or `invalid`; no legacy aliases and no `frusta/all`, `frusta/top_oracle`, or `frusta/invalid`.
  - Add configurable subset controls: `all`, `valid_only`, `invalid_only`, `top_k_oracle`, and explicit candidate indices.
  - Selected detail candidate defaults to top valid oracle RRI, with config and CLI override by explicit candidate index.
  - Candidate depth and candidate point cloud logging becomes selected-only by default; remove first/middle/last arbitrary depth windows.
  - Candidate metrics move into a candidate table plus an RRI histogram using native `rr.BarChart`.

- Geometry and modalities:
  - Log candidate frusta with `rr.Transform3D(relation=ParentFromChild)` and `rr.Pinhole(camera_xyz=rr.ViewCoordinates.LUF)` on each candidate camera entity.
  - Log selected candidate `DepthImage(meter=1.0)` under the selected camera branch.
  - Convert GT and detected OBBs to native `rr.Boxes3D`; keep snippet-to-world conversion and CW90/display-only boundaries explicit.
  - Log VIN offline time-collapsed semidense points with quality coloring where field alignment is reliable.
  - Log EFM voxel `occ_pr`, `cent_pr`, and `cent_pr_nms` as spatialized thresholded/capped `Points3D` using `t_world_voxel` and `voxel_extent`.
  - Summarize remaining raw fields in metadata for v1: `bbox_pr`, `clas_pr`, calibration, exposure/gain, frame IDs, timestamps, raw `gt_data`, and absent invalid-reason/counterfactual fields.

- Config/API:
  - Add candidate-detail config for selected strategy, explicit selected index, subset mode, top-k, and explicit index list.
  - Add EFM voxel config for per-field thresholds, max point caps, and enable flags.
  - Add ASE camera keyframe config fixed by default to RGB image plus RGB depth for first and last trajectory frame only.
  - Update smoke config and generated RRD target to use the new tree.

## Test Plan
- Update logger tests to assert the new semantic paths and no legacy candidate aggregate paths.
- Add tests for all-candidate native camera logging grouped by validity, selected-only depth/points, explicit selected-index override, and all-invalid behavior.
- Add tests for `world/gt/mesh`, `world/ase/*`, `world/efm/*`, native `Boxes3D`, native `Pinhole`, metric depth, and `rr.BarChart` histogram calls.
- Regenerate a real-data `.rrd` smoke artifact and inspect its entity tree with `rerun rrd print`.
- Run targeted checks: `pytest aria_nbv/tests/rerun_inspector aria_nbv/tests/data_handling/test_offline_visual_inventory.py -q` and `ruff check aria_nbv/aria_nbv/rerun_inspector aria_nbv/tests/rerun_inspector`.

## Assumptions
- No compatibility aliases for old Rerun paths.
- EFM and EVL are treated as one display domain named `efm`.
- v1 prioritizes curated spatial diagnostics over dumping every raw tensor.
- Candidate native cameras may create ~60 entities per sample; this is acceptable for inspector trust diagnostics.

`. - Fall back to `class=` when the semantic id is missing or out of range. - Preserve current native `rr.Boxes3D` rendering. - Streamline `nbv-rerun-inspect`. - Add `--view`: generate/save the `.rrd`, then run native `rerun ` in the foreground. - Add `--serve-web`: generate/save the `.rrd`, then run `rerun --serve-web ` in the foreground. - Add `--web-viewer-port` and `--ws-server-port`, defaulting to `0` for OS-selected free ports. - Add `--lan`: only for `--serve-web`; bind Rerun to `0.0.0.0`, detect the host LAN IP, and print a LAN URL hint. - Default safe bind remains `127.0.0.1`; other devices on the network require `--lan`. - Pass through Rerun stdout/stderr so its native “open this URL” output remains visible; for `--lan`, append an ARIA-NBV hint using the detected host IP when the web port is explicit or parsed from Rerun output. - Treat `--view` and `--serve-web` as mutually exclusive and incompatible with SDK `--spawn`/`--connect`. ## CLI Examples ```bash uv run nbv-rerun-inspect \ --config-path ../.configs/rerun_offline_smoke_v6.toml \ --split val \ --index 0 \ --save ../.artifacts/rerun/offline_smoke_v6.rrd \ --view ``` ```bash uv run nbv-rerun-inspect \ --config-path ../.configs/rerun_offline_smoke_v6.toml \ --split val \ --index 0 \ --save ../.artifacts/rerun/offline_smoke_v6.rrd \ --serve-web \ --lan ``` ## Test Plan - Add logger tests for: - `world/efm/voxels/extent` exists when backbone voxel pose/extent exist. - extent box center/half-size are computed correctly from the configured extent. - GT and detected OBB labels include class names from `sem_id_to_name`. - unknown semantic ids fall back cleanly. - Add CLI tests for: - `--view` builds the expected foreground `rerun ` command. - `--serve-web` uses auto ports by default. - explicit web/ws ports are passed through. - `--lan` changes bind to `0.0.0.0`. - invalid flag combinations fail before generation/viewer launch. - Regenerate `.artifacts/rerun/offline_smoke_v6.rrd` and inspect with `rerun rrd print`. ## Assumptions - The path is `world/efm/voxels/extent`, not `world/efm/obbs/voxel_extent`. - Viewer subprocesses run in the foreground by default. - Port defaults use Rerun’s native `0` auto-selection behavior. - LAN exposure is opt-in via `--lan` for safety.

# Alignment Plan: Thesis Scope And Next Edits

## Summary
Revise the thesis plan from “bounded rollouts before optional RL” to a harder gated core:

- **System name:** `ARIA-NBV`.
- **Core claim:** target-conditioned, quality-driven NBV on ASE/EFM with strict M1 contracts.
- **Mandatory hard deliverable:** target-conditioned **multi-step fitted Double-Q / Q_H** over finite candidate sets, trained from ASE oracle rollout data.
- **Simulator substrate:** ASE mesh/oracle counterfactual rollout loop, not Habitat/Isaac.
- **Success bar:** learned Q_H beats one-step greedy/model scoring on cumulative target RRI under equal acquisition budget; oracle lookahead is an upper bound.
- **Final scale bar:** full 100 GT-mesh ASE scenes / 4,608 snippets is mandatory for final experiments, after small-subset correctness.

## Key Changes To Plan Into Docs/DB
- Update `roadmap.qmd`, `questions.qmd`, `DECISIONS.md`, and relevant agents DB records.
- Replace current three-tier boundary with four tiers:
  - implemented substrate;
  - prerequisite core: proposal, M1, V0/V1 target contracts, rollout storage;
  - hard thesis core: observed-only auto target selector, predicted target-conditioned scorer/Q_H, greedy+softmax+Gumbel rollouts, fitted Double Q, full-scale LRZ generation;
  - stretch: IQL second ablation, actor-critic bridge, continuous policies, Habitat/Isaac, SceneScript, real-device guidance.
- Move Q_H from late M6 stretch/gate into **M5 mandatory deliverable**.
- Make M6 an actor-critic/continuous-policy bridge only, not a required quantitative continuous baseline.
- Mark LRZ deterministic sharding/storage/Slurm/DSS as a hard M2/M3 gate before full-scale generation.

## Core Contracts
- **Target contract:** GT OBB defines target RRI crop/evaluation; observed/predicted OBB is actor-visible input.
  - V0: GT OBB input + GT label crop for sanity/upper bound.
  - V1 mandatory: observed/predicted OBB input + matched GT OBB target-RRI label.
  - Main protocol name: `OBS-SEL / PRED-Q / GT-EVAL`.
- **Target selector:** mandatory observed-only automatic selector using predicted OBBs/classes/confidence, projected area, and current semidense/EVL point support. GT is label/evaluation only.
- **Matching rule:** compatible class + IoU + visibility/support; projected area + points are first support signals; extra criterion `X` remains deferred.
- **Candidate generation:** mandatory mixed observed candidate set with categorical-probability hyperparameters for strategy selection; includes default exploration, predicted-target LookAt, random/forward; GT LookAt is upper-bound only.
- **Invalidity:** hard masks + explicit reason codes are mandatory; validity heads/penalty rewards are ablations.
- **Reward/Q:** Q_H predicts bounded cumulative target RRI. Scalar motion/rule penalties are extensions.
- **Rollout data:** random-valid, greedy, bounded oracle lookahead, temperature-softmax, and Gumbel-Top-k with per-step branch schedules must be stable before Q_H training.
- **Q algorithm:** fitted Double-Q first; IQL second offline-RL ablation; SB3 DQN only after an online Gymnasium simulator exists.
- **Storage:** Zarr-first rollout/Q store, rich enough for training/evaluation without duplicating raw ASE/ATEK. Full meshes are external path/hash/version references; high-detail target mesh crops are embedded once per target with crop metadata.

## Evidence And Verification Plan
- Proposal freeze first, then M1.
- Track generated `proposal.pdf` in git once frozen.
- Bibliography must use primary metadata: remove Wikipedia/generated slop, deduplicate FiLM, verify recent papers through primary pages/arXiv/DOI/Semantic Scholar.
- M1 is a hard stop before target/RL scaling:
  - public `docs/contents/thesis/m1_contract_report.qmd`;
  - data/store/split/frame/CW90/candidate-order/depth-backprojection evidence;
  - Rerun normal/boundary/failure recordings;
  - targeted tests and oracle throughput.
- Final experiments use scene-level splits; held-out test split remains advisor decision.
- CI/pre-commit becomes required before full-scale generation, not before proposal/M1.
- GitHub issue mirroring remains a local TODO only.

## Assumptions And Deferred Decisions
- Full GT coverage is mandatory, but implementation starts with a small trusted subset.
- Actor-visible target input must become predicted/observed OBB for the main result.
- Continuous actor-critic is not required as a quantitative thesis result; only the bridge design is required.
- Deferred decisions: target matching criterion `X`, final test split, exact Zarr group layout, exact Q_H thresholds/metrics, and IQL scope.

# Resolve `questions.qmd` Inline TODOs

## Summary
Revise `docs/contents/thesis/questions.qmd` to remove the inline TODOs while preserving the current 8-RQ structure. The resolved thesis framing is: `ARIA-NBV` first proves target-centric quality-driven NBV with a quality-only cumulative target-RRI baseline, then treats fitted finite-candidate `Q_H` as the mandatory multi-step policy question in RQ5.

## Key Changes
- Rewrite RQ1 as the broad target-centric NBV objective question: cumulative target-specific RRI over multi-step finite candidate choices in complex ASE indoor scenes.
- Keep acquisition/motion/validity penalties out of the main RQ1 objective; report them as diagnostics or later scalarized ablations after the quality-only baseline is stable.
- Rewrite RQ2 to explicitly state that actor-visible target inputs come from the employed egocentric foundation model: predicted/tracked OBBs, class probabilities, confidence, projected area, and semidense/EVL support.
- Split RQ2 into target descriptors versus encodings: descriptors are OBB/class/support signals; encodings include relative target pose, R6D-style orientation, translation/extent features, class-probability embeddings, and LFF/MLP encoders.
- Align RQ3 with the existing ARIA-NBV candidate-generation package as thesis-core vocabulary: `RADIAL_AWAY`, `RADIAL_TOWARDS`, `TARGET_POINT`, `FORWARD_RIG`, `UNIFORM_SPHERE`, `FORWARD_POWERSPHERICAL`, and existing yaw/pitch/roll jitter. Frontier or missing-surface sampling remains stretch unless implemented.
- De-prioritize RQ4 by making it only about target-conditioned one-step scoring. Remove `Q_H` from RQ4 and keep fitted Double-Q / bounded multi-step policy success entirely in RQ5.
- Update the research-question matrix so RQ4 is a scorer prerequisite/diagnostic and RQ5 is the mandatory learned multi-step policy result.

## Glossary And Memory
- Add glossary entries in `docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ` for:
  - `OBS-SEL`: observed-only target selection using predicted/tracked OBBs and support signals; GT is not actor-visible.
  - `PRED-Q`: predicted/observed target descriptors are used by the scorer or `Q_H` model.
  - `GT-EVAL`: GT OBB/mesh crops are used only for oracle labels and evaluation.
- Regenerate glossary artifacts with `make glossary`; do not hand-edit generated glossary outputs.
- Update `.agents/memory/state/DECISIONS.md` only where needed to record the locked decisions: RQ4 scorer-only split, quality-only baseline first, and package-supported candidate modes as the core thesis candidate vocabulary.
- Add a normal debrief under `.agents/memory/history/YYYY/MM/` with `canonical_updates_needed` recorded.

## Verification
- Run `make glossary`.
- Run `cd docs && quarto render contents/thesis/questions.qmd`.
- Run `cd docs && quarto render contents/glossary.qmd`.
- Run `make check-agent-memory` if memory or debrief files are changed.
- Run `git diff --check -- docs/contents/thesis/questions.qmd docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ .agents/memory/state/DECISIONS.md`.

## Assumptions
- Keep the 8 research questions; do not renumber.
- Do not edit `docs/typst/thesis/proposal.typ` in this pass.
- Do not create GitHub issues.
- This is a docs/memory alignment pass only; no candidate-generation code changes are required.

# Math-Heavy Tiered Glossary Lookup

## Summary
Convert the glossary into a thesis math lookup surface: core concepts and symbols first, supporting/background concepts still linkable but visually demoted. Add the ARIA-NBV MDP contract as a core glossary concept set, with formulas for state, finite candidate actions, transition, reward, finite-horizon return, `Q_H`, and validity masks.

## Key Changes
- Extend the glossary metadata/rendering path:
  - Add optional fields to glossary metadata: `tier`, `lookup_rank`, `symbol_refs`, and `equation_refs`.
  - Supported tiers: `core`, `support`, `background`.
  - Render a “Core Math Lookup” table before the category cards, sorted by `lookup_rank`.
  - Show tier badges on all cards; keep existing anchors and term IDs stable.
  - Preserve generated artifacts by editing only `docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ` and `scripts/glossary_build.py`, then running `make glossary`.

- Add or enrich core MDP terms:
  - `target-conditioned-nbv-mdp`: finite-horizon ARIA-NBV MDP contract.
  - `rollout-state`: actor-visible state, e.g. accumulated points, candidates, masks, target descriptor, history, and budget.
  - `finite-candidate-action-set`: masked action set over sampled candidate views.
  - `counterfactual-transition`: candidate observation/render/fusion update.
  - `target-rri-reward`: main quality-only target-RRI reward, with log-improvement marked as follow-up/ablation.
  - `finite-horizon-return`: symbolic discounted return with `gamma`; thesis comparisons default to cumulative target RRI.
  - `finite-horizon-q-function`: `Q_H` over finite candidates.
  - `validity-mask`: hard candidate mask and invalid reason semantics.

- Add shared symbols/equations for the lookup:
  - Core symbols: `s_t`, `q_{t,i}`, `Q_t`, `A(s_t)`, `m_{t,i}`, `rho_{t,i}`, `P_t`, `P_q`, `M_GT`, `M_e`, `RRI_e`, `r_t^e`, `G_t^(H)`, `Q_H`, `gamma`, `H`, and transition `T`.
  - Core formulas:
    - `M_NBV = (S, A, T, r_e, gamma, H)`
    - `A(s_t) = {q_{t,i} in Q_t : m_{t,i}=1}`
    - `P_{t+1} = P_t union P_{q_t}`
    - `r_t^e = RRI_e(q_t | P_t, M_e)`
    - `G_t^(H) = sum_{k=0}^{H-1} gamma^k r_{t+k}^e`
    - `Q_H(s_t,q) = E[G_t^(H) | s_t, a_t=q]`
  - Add notation entries to `docs/notation.yml` so Quarto/Typst/KG outputs share the same symbol registry.

- Tier existing terms:
  - `core`: NBV, RRI, target RRI, CD, candidate view, target/protocol terms, oracle RRI, target-conditioned scorer, acquisition cost, point cloud/current reconstruction, and the new MDP terms.
  - `support`: ASE, EFM3D, EVL, OBB, frustum, LUF, SLAM, VIN, coverage ratio, occupancy grid.
  - `background`: ADT, AEO, VRS, MPS, CPF, MFCD/MTD/MSDPD, SceneScript, MVS, VIO/track, and generic DoF terms unless directly used in core formulas.

- Minimal doc alignment:
  - Update `docs/contents/theory/rl_planning.qmd` and `docs/contents/thesis/roadmap.qmd` only where needed so they state: cumulative target RRI is the main thesis reward/return; log-improvement remains a follow-up/ablation to explore.
  - Do not do a broad theory-page rewrite in this pass.
  - Update `DECISIONS.md` only if the new glossary tiering and reward convention need canonical state capture.

## Test Scenarios
- Normal case: an advisor looking up `Q_H` sees the formula, linked MDP state/action/reward terms, and the relevant symbols without reading the full RL page.
- Boundary case: a background dataset term such as ADT remains linkable but no longer competes with MDP/RRI terms in the top lookup.
- Failure case: invalid candidates are represented through masks/reasons in the glossary, not as low target-RRI examples.

## Verification
- `make glossary`
- `cd docs && quarto render contents/glossary.qmd contents/theory/rl_planning.qmd contents/thesis/roadmap.qmd`
- `make check-agent-memory` if `.agents/memory/state` or a debrief is changed
- `git diff --check -- docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ scripts/glossary_build.py docs/notation.yml docs/contents/theory/rl_planning.qmd docs/contents/thesis/roadmap.qmd`
- Optional: `make qmd-frontmatter-check`, noting the existing unrelated `docs/contents/ideas.qmd` metadata failure if still present.

## Assumptions
- Keep all existing glossary term IDs stable; demotion changes presentation, not linkability.
- Main reward is cumulative target RRI; log-improvement is explicitly marked as future exploration.
- Keep `gamma` symbolic in formulas; use cumulative/equal-budget target-RRI as the thesis-core comparison.
- No `proposal.typ` edits and no GitHub issue creation in this pass.

# Make litkg-rs Agent-Useful for ARIA-NBV

## Summary
- Keep litkg-rs as the structural KG/retrieval layer, but fix trust first: freshness, authority, backlog coverage, and source typing.
- Current KG snapshot: 75 registry records, 785 parsed records, 8,209 Neo4j nodes, 13,034 edges, 1,518 code symbols, 86 project-memory nodes, 41 Semantic Scholar-enriched records.
- Main risk: `kg find` can return stale or wrongly typed evidence, while `context-pack` reads fresher live sources. Agents could cite outdated project truth.

## Key Changes
- Fix stale export handling in [main.rs](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/external/litkg-rs/crates/litkg-cli/src/main.rs:1130): `kg find` only rebuilds Neo4j export when missing, not when source files are newer. Add freshness checks or emit hard warnings before search.
- Fix authority ranking in [context_pack.rs](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/external/litkg-rs/crates/litkg-core/src/context_pack.rs:333): it passes absolute paths into [ranking.rs](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/external/litkg-rs/crates/litkg-core/src/ranking.rs:26), so relative `.configs/litkg.toml` authority tiers often do not match.
- Add real backlog graph export. Capabilities advertises `AgentBacklogIssue` / `AgentBacklogTodo` in [inspect.rs](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/external/litkg-rs/crates/litkg-core/src/inspect.rs:969), but `kg find --modality backlog litkg` returns `0`.
- Apply authority/freshness ranking to `kg find`, not only context-pack. [query.rs](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/external/litkg-rs/crates/litkg-viewer/src/query.rs:476) currently ranks mostly by lexical matches and title/id/path scores.
- Split document types more cleanly: debriefs, generated docs, memory, public docs, and actual literature are currently often surfaced as `Paper` / `PaperSection`, which pollutes “literature” results.
- Add `kg-consolidate`: proposal-only output for PROJECT_STATE, DECISIONS, OPEN_QUESTIONS, GOTCHAS, and agents-db updates, backed by cited evidence.
- Add experiment evidence ingestion after the experiment registry exists: run IDs, config hashes, split manifests, cache/store IDs, metrics, figures, and supported claims.

## Test Plan
- `kg find --modality backlog litkg` returns current issue/todo nodes.
- `kg find "current thesis spine"` matches the live 2026-05-05 PROJECT_STATE text, not stale exported text.
- `context-pack` and `kg find` both expose `authority`, `freshness`, `source_type`, `score_final`, and `why`.
- Canonical memory and current code outrank old debriefs for comparable matches.
- `kg-claim-check` flags unsupported overclaims like “ARIA-NBV is a finished end-to-end RL policy.”
- Retrieval benchmark: create ARIA-NBV RepoQA questions covering RRI, VIN, rollout, cache, LRZ, docs, and KG workflows.

## Assumptions
- Graphify/JSONL remains the durable default; Neo4j/Graphiti are optional runtime layers.
- MemPalace stays separate episodic mining, not the structural litkg backend.
- No automatic canonical memory edits; consolidation should emit reviewable patches.

# Literature Review Cleanup Plan

## Summary

Rewrite the literature review into a concise, source-backed, domain-based structure with an adoption-state overview. The goal is to remove AI slop, preserve only thesis-relevant signals, cross-check claims against local paper sources through litkg-rs, and integrate glossary shortcodes consistently.

Use the hierarchy chosen in review:

1. NBV objective and candidate planning
2. ARIA ecosystem and actor-visible state
3. Rollout, value learning, and RL
4. 3DGS / radiance-field active reconstruction
5. Semantic scene representations

The index page should give a compact overview plus an adoption-state table.

## Key Changes

- Rewrite `docs/contents/literature/index.qmd` around domain sections and a table with columns:
  `domain`, `papers`, `adoption state`, `core signal`, `do not adopt`.
- Use adoption states consistently:
  `core substrate`, `thesis-core method`, `proposal/diagnostic`, `gated follow-up`, `stretch/bridge`, `background`.
- Apply one concise page template to literature pages:
  `Core contribution`, `Verified paper signals`, `ARIA-NBV adoption`, `Do not adopt`, `Open risks / caveats`.
- Prune or rewrite the highest-slop pages first:
  `vin_nbv.qmd`, `efm3d.qmd`, `gen_nbv.qmd`, `scene_script.qmd`.
- Keep the already cleaner pages but normalize style and glossary usage:
  `project_aria.qmd`, `pb_nbv.qmd`, `rl_planning.qmd`, `active_3dgs_nbv.qmd`, `hestia.qmd`.

## Formatting And Structure Rules

- Replace pseudo-equation text with valid TeX display math. For example:
  ```tex
  $$
  Q_H(s_t, q_t, z_e)
  \approx
  \mathbb{E}\!\left[
    \sum_{k=0}^{H-1-t} \gamma^k r^{\mathrm{target}}_{t+k}
    \mid s_t, q_t, z_e
  \right].
  $$
  ```
- Replace text-arrow pipelines with valid Mermaid diagrams using Quarto `{mermaid}` fences.
- Remove ` ```text` blocks used as visual structure in literature pages; use tables, bullets, TeX, or Mermaid instead.
- Use `{{< gls ... >}}` / `{{< glsfull ... >}}` for durable terms such as NBV, RRI, target RRI, ASE, EFM3D, EVL, MPS, OBB, candidate view, oracle RRI, Q_H protocol terms, and validity masks.
- Add only minimal new glossary terms where durable and missing, likely `Project Aria` and `3D Gaussian Splatting`; do not add a glossary entry for every paper.

## Source-Check Requirements

- Use litkg-rs before editing:
  `make kg-query KG_QUERY='review and restructure ARIA-NBV literature reviews with source checks' LITKG_PROFILE=docs-paper-sync KG_FORMAT=text`
- Cross-check every factual claim against the local source when available:
  VIN-NBV, GenNBV, EFM3D, Project Aria, SceneScript, PB-NBV, Hestia, Trajectory Transformer, Double DQN, IQL, Deep Energy-Based Policies, Gumbel-Top-k, Next Best Sense, Dynamic 3DGS, Instance/Object-centric NBV.
- For FOV-HPE, state that the corpus has DOI/PDF evidence but no local TeX mirror.
- Remove or soften unsupported claims, especially “first”, exact percentage claims, hardware/training claims, and broad “outperforms” statements unless directly supported by the paper source.

## Page-Specific Plan

- `vin_nbv.qmd`: keep RRI, oracle labels, CORAL ordinal training, greedy candidate ranking, benchmark caveats, and transfer to ARIA-NBV. Remove emojis, “??”, “Our Approach” drift, and overbroad RL/imitation claims.
- `efm3d.qmd`: make it a concise Project Aria/ASE/EVL literature distillation. Move useful EVL feature-selection/debug-dictionary material into `docs/contents/impl/vin_v2_feature_proposals.qmd` as implementation guidance; remove chatty “you printed” prose.
- `gen_nbv.qmd`: source-check 5-DoF action, PPO, state embedding, coverage reward, Houses3K/OmniObject3D results, and limitations. Remove Wikipedia dependency and dismissive wording.
- `scene_script.qmd`: cut duplicated “key insight” sections and keep the relevant signals: structured scene language, ASE scale, MPS point cloud input, editable semantic representation, and stretch-only semantic/global planning role.
- `rl_planning.qmd`: expand around local RL papers:
  Trajectory Transformer for sequence/beam planning, Gumbel-Top-k for stochastic beams without replacement, Double DQN for overestimation control, IQL for in-dataset offline RL, Deep Energy-Based Policies for maximum-entropy/soft candidate distributions, plus PPO/SAC only as simulator-gated bridges.
- `active_3dgs_nbv.qmd`: preserve concise method cards but replace text blocks with a table and source-check local TeX/PDF-backed claims.
- Sidebar order in `docs/_quarto.yml` should match the new domain hierarchy.

## Verification

- `make kg-query KG_QUERY='source-check ARIA-NBV literature review rewrite' LITKG_PROFILE=docs-paper-sync KG_FORMAT=text`
- `make glossary` if glossary source changes.
- `make qmd-frontmatter-check`
- Render touched pages individually:
  `cd docs && quarto render contents/literature/index.qmd contents/literature/vin_nbv.qmd contents/literature/efm3d.qmd contents/literature/gen_nbv.qmd contents/literature/scene_script.qmd contents/literature/rl_planning.qmd contents/literature/active_3dgs_nbv.qmd`
- If Mermaid diagrams are added or substantially changed, validate them with Mermaid CLI before final render.
- Run searches before finishing:
  `rg '```text|~=|✅|⚠️|\\?\\?|You’re|Our Approach|Wikipedia' docs/contents/literature`
  and resolve every hit unless it is intentionally retained and justified.

## Assumptions

- Do not edit `proposal.typ`, roadmap, questions, agents DB, or litkg-rs implementation in this pass.
- Do not touch unrelated dirty worktree changes.
- Keep literature pages public-facing and thesis-oriented; implementation detail belongs under `docs/contents/impl/`.
- `Q_H` remains mandatory M5 thesis-core work, while IQL, actor-critic, SB3/PPO/SAC, Habitat/Isaac, and 3DGS control remain gated follow-up or stretch work.

# Mac-Offloaded Ollama for ARIA-NBV litkg Refresh

## Summary
- Keep ARIA-NBV sources, durable litkg artifacts, CodeGraphContext, Graphiti, and Neo4j on the Ubuntu workstation.
- Use the Mac only as the Ollama model server over an SSH reverse tunnel.
- Pin litkg runtime model use to:
  - `EMBEDDING_MODEL=qwen3-embedding:4b`
  - `GRAPHITI_LLM_MODEL=gemma4:26b`
- Make remote Ollama a first-class supported path instead of requiring the Ubuntu host to have a local `ollama` CLI.

## Key Changes
- Add an Ollama HTTP helper layer to the litkg-rs KG scripts:
  - Query models through `GET /api/tags`.
  - Verify required models are present before ingestion/enrichment.
  - Use existing HTTP endpoints for `/api/embed` and `/api/chat`.
  - Fail fast with a clear message if `qwen3-embedding:4b` or `gemma4:26b` is missing.
  - Do not silently fall back to another Gemma model.
- Update `ingest_docs.sh`:
  - Remove hard dependency on a local Ubuntu `ollama` CLI when `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` is reachable.
  - Default `GRAPHITI_LLM_MODEL` to `gemma4:26b`.
  - Default `EMBEDDING_MODEL` to `qwen3-embedding:4b`.
  - Keep `uv`, Graphiti checkout, Neo4j, and document ingestion running on Ubuntu.
- Update `enrich_embeddings.py`:
  - Replace local `ollama list` / `ollama pull` assumptions with HTTP model verification.
  - Use `gemma4:26b` for token-filter chat when available through `GRAPHITI_LLM_MODEL`.
  - Preserve `qwen3-embedding:4b` and `EMBEDDING_DIM=1024` for node embeddings and vector index compatibility.
- Add operator-facing configuration:
  - Update litkg-rs `.env.example` defaults to `gemma4:26b`.
  - Add ARIA-NBV docs or helper comments showing the SSH command:
    ```bash
    ssh -R 11434:127.0.0.1:11434 jd@ubuntu-workstation
    ```
  - Ubuntu-side env:
    ```bash
    export OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
    export OLLAMA_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:11434
    export EMBEDDING_MODEL=qwen3-embedding:4b
    export GRAPHITI_LLM_MODEL=gemma4:26b
    ```
- Add a preflight target, preferably `make kg-ollama-check`, that validates:
  - Tunnel is reachable from Ubuntu.
  - Both required models are installed on the Mac.
  - Embedding endpoint returns 1024-dimensional vectors.
  - Chat endpoint returns a valid response for `gemma4:26b`.

## Refresh Workflow
- Mac:
  ```bash
  ollama serve
  ollama pull qwen3-embedding:4b
  ollama pull gemma4:26b
  ssh -R 11434:127.0.0.1:11434 jd@ubuntu-workstation
  ```
- Ubuntu:

  - Normalizes `/v1` and non-`/v1` base URLs.
- Script preflight tests:
  - `kg-ollama-check` succeeds through the SSH reverse tunnel.

- Runtime smoke:
  - `make kg-ingest-docs` uses `gemma4:26b` from the Mac, not a local Ubuntu model.
  - `enrich_embeddings.py` writes `kg_embedding_model=qwen3-embedding:4b`.

- Existing verification:

  - In ARIA-NBV: `make kg-capabilities KG_FORMAT=json` and `make check-agent-memory`.

## Assumptions
- SSH reverse tunnel is the supported default.
- Ubuntu remains the authoritative host for source paths, generated KG artifacts, Neo4j, and Graphiti state.
- The Mac already has enough memory for `gemma4:26b`; concurrency should stay conservative with `SEMAPHORE_LIMIT=1` or `2`.
- Scripts should verify required remote models, not auto-pull them from Ubuntu.

❯ cat ~/.ssh/config
Host ubuntu ubuntu-ws
  User jd
  Port 22
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_ubuntu_ws
  IdentitiesOnly yes
  HostKeyAlias ubuntu-workstation
  CheckHostIP no
  ProxyCommand ~/.ssh/ubuntu-proxy %p
  AddressFamily inet
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IgnoreUnknown UseKeychain
  ServerAliveInterval 30
  ServerAliveCountMax 3
  ControlMaster no

PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Ext-Impl Cleanup And Implementation Docs Restructure Plan

## Summary
Archive noisy `docs/contents/ext-impl/*.qmd` pages, retain only a compact internal ATEK/EFM3D/Project Aria developer reference, and clean public docs so implementation chapters support the thesis-evidence path instead of exposing vendor dumps.

Decisions locked:
- Raw `ext-impl` pages become deprecated archive material under `.agents/archive/docs/ext-impl/`.
- Retained high-value facts live in `.agents/references/external_stack_contracts.md`.
- Public docs use thesis-evidence grouping and public-only glossary links.
- No Python docstring edits in this pass; create an agents-db todo for that follow-up.

## Key Changes
- Archive and mark deprecated:
  - Move `atek_implementation.qmd`, `efm3d_implementation.qmd`, `efm3d_symbol_index.qmd`, and `prj_aria_tools_impl.qmd` to `.agents/archive/docs/ext-impl/`.
  - Add archive frontmatter/note: historical, deprecated, not current guidance, use `.agents/references/external_stack_contracts.md` for distilled developer guidance.
  - Remove the public `External Implementations` sidebar section and homepage section.

- Add internal developer reference:
  - Create `.agents/references/external_stack_contracts.md`.
  - Keep ATEK contracts: WDS loading/remap, semidense/trajectory/calibration fields, surface metric helpers, GT/OBB support relevant to target RRI.
  - Keep EFM3D contracts: `PoseTW`, `CameraTW`, `ObbTW`, consumed `ARIA_*` keys, `EfmModelAdaptor`, ray/depth/pointcloud/mesh utilities, EVL evidence limits.
  - Add only a short Project Aria Tools note for VRS/MPS/ASE provenance.
  - Prune examples, Wikipedia primers, exhaustive symbol tables, terminal trees, tutorial code, CubeRCNN/SAM2 side paths, and speculative “underused” lists.

- Public docs and glossary:
  - Regroup the implementation sidebar around thesis evidence: system/package, data-oracle-diagnostics, and scorer/training.
  - Do not rewrite large implementation pages now, but remove direct links to archived `ext-impl` pages.
  - Replace glossary internal links to `docs/contents/ext-impl/efm3d_implementation.qmd` with public literature/API targets only.
  - Update generated glossary outputs via `make glossary`.

- Agents DB:
  - Amend `todo-001` and `refactor-004` to record the `ext-impl` cleanup and public/internal boundary.
  - Add new `todo-054` for targeted package docstring enrichment from `external_stack_contracts.md`.
  - Link the new todo to `issue-003`, `issue-007`, and `issue-010`.

## Test Plan
- Validate docs/backlog:
  - `make agents-db AGENTS_ARGS='validate'`
  - `make agents-db`
  - `make glossary`
  - `make qmd-frontmatter-check`
  - `make check-agent-memory`

- Render touched public pages:
  - `cd docs && quarto render index.qmd contents/glossary.qmd contents/impl/overview.qmd contents/theory/surface_metrics.qmd`

- Search for stale public references:
  - `rg 'contents/ext-impl|External Implementations|ProjectAria Tools Reference|EFM3D Symbol Index|ATEK Implementation Index|EFM3D Implementation Index' docs README.md -g '!_site/**'`
  - Expected result: no public-doc links to archived `ext-impl` pages.

## Assumptions
- Do not edit `roadmap.qmd`, `questions.qmd`, `proposal.typ`, or Python source in this pass.
- Do not touch unrelated dirty worktree files.
- Keep archived raw QMD files out of public Quarto rendering.
- Broader cleanup of noisy `docs/contents/impl/*.qmd` pages remains follow-up work under the existing docs-pruning backlog.

description: "Use when the user asks how to build with OpenAI products or APIs and needs up-to-date official documentation with citations, help choosing the latest model for a use case, or model upgrade and prompt-upgrade guidance; prioritize OpenAI docs MCP tools, use bundled references only as helper context, and restrict any fallback browsing to official OpenAI domains."
---


# OpenAI Docs

Provide authoritative, current guidance from OpenAI developer docs using the developers.openai.com MCP server. Always prioritize the developer docs MCP tools over web.run for OpenAI-related questions. This skill also owns model selection, API model migration, and prompt-upgrade guidance. Only if the MCP server is installed and returns no meaningful results should you fall back to web search.

## Quick start

- Use `mcp__openaiDeveloperDocs__search_openai_docs` to find the most relevant doc pages.
- Use `mcp__openaiDeveloperDocs__fetch_openai_doc` to pull exact sections and quote/paraphrase accurately.
- Use `mcp__openaiDeveloperDocs__list_openai_docs` only when you need to browse or discover pages without a clear query.
- For model-selection, "latest model", or default-model questions, fetch `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md` first. If that is unavailable, load `references/latest-model.md`.
- For model upgrades or prompt upgrades, run `node scripts/resolve-latest-model-info.js` only when the target is latest/current/default or otherwise unspecified; otherwise preserve the explicitly requested target.
- Preserve explicit target requests: if the user names a target model like "migrate to GPT-5.4", keep that requested target even if `latest-model.md` names a newer model. Mention newer guidance only as optional.
- If current remote guidance is needed, fetch both the returned migration and prompting guide URLs directly. If direct fetch fails, use MCP/search fallback; if that also fails, use bundled fallback references and disclose the fallback.

## OpenAI product snapshots

1. Apps SDK: Build ChatGPT apps by providing a web component UI and an MCP server that exposes your app's tools to ChatGPT.
2. Responses API: A unified endpoint designed for stateful, multimodal, tool-using interactions in agentic workflows.
3. Chat Completions API: Generate a model response from a list of messages comprising a conversation.
4. Codex: OpenAI's coding agent for software development that can write, understand, review, and debug code.
5. gpt-oss: Open-weight OpenAI reasoning models (gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b) released under the Apache 2.0 license.
6. Realtime API: Build low-latency, multimodal experiences including natural speech-to-speech conversations.
7. Agents SDK: A toolkit for building agentic apps where a model can use tools and context, hand off to other agents, stream partial results, and keep a full trace.

## If MCP server is missing

If MCP tools fail or no OpenAI docs resources are available:

1. Run the install command yourself: `codex mcp add openaiDeveloperDocs --url https://developers.openai.com/mcp`
2. If it fails due to permissions/sandboxing, immediately retry the same command with escalated permissions and include a 1-sentence justification for approval. Do not ask the user to run it yet.
3. Only if the escalated attempt fails, ask the user to run the install command.
4. Ask the user to restart Codex.
5. Re-run the doc search/fetch after restart.

## Workflow

1. Clarify whether the request is general docs lookup, model selection, a model-string upgrade, prompt-upgrade guidance, or broader API/provider migration.
2. For model-selection or upgrade requests, prefer current remote docs over bundled references when the user asks for latest/current/default guidance.
   - Fetch `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md`.
   - Find the latest model ID and explicit migration or prompt-guidance links.
   - Prefer explicit links from the latest-model page over derived URLs.
   - For explicit named-model requests, preserve the requested model target and do not silently retarget to the latest model. Mention newer remote guidance only as optional.
   - For dynamic latest/current/default upgrades, run `node scripts/resolve-latest-model-info.js`, then fetch both returned guide URLs directly when possible.
   - If direct guide fetch fails, use the developer-docs MCP tools or official OpenAI-domain search to find the same guide content.
   - If remote docs are unavailable, use bundled fallback references and say that fallback guidance was used.
3. For model upgrades, keep changes narrow: update active OpenAI API model defaults and directly related prompts only when safe.
4. Leave historical docs, examples, eval baselines, fixtures, provider comparisons, provider registries, pricing tables, alias defaults, low-cost fallback paths, and ambiguous older model usage unchanged unless the user explicitly asks to upgrade them.
5. Do not perform SDK, tooling, IDE, plugin, shell, auth, or provider-environment migrations as part of a model-and-prompt upgrade.
6. If an upgrade needs API-surface changes, schema rewiring, tool-handler changes, or implementation work beyond a literal model-string replacement and prompt edits, report it as blocked or confirmation-needed.
7. For general docs lookup, search docs with a precise query, fetch the best page and exact section needed, and answer with concise citations.

## Reference map

Read only what you need:

- `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.md` -> current model-selection and "best/latest/current model" questions.
- `references/latest-model.md` -> bundled fallback for model-selection and "best/latest/current model" questions.
- `references/upgrade-guide.md` -> bundled fallback for model upgrade and upgrade-planning requests.
- `references/prompting-guide.md` -> bundled fallback for prompt rewrites and prompt-behavior upgrades.

## Quality rules

- Treat OpenAI docs as the source of truth; avoid speculation.
- Keep migration changes narrow and behavior-preserving.
- Prefer prompt-only upgrades when possible.
- Do not invent pricing, availability, parameters, API changes, or breaking changes.
- Keep quotes short and within policy limits; prefer paraphrase with citations.
- If multiple pages differ, call out the difference and cite both.
- If official docs and repo behavior disagree, state the conflict and stop before making broad edits.
- If docs do not cover the user’s need, say so and offer next steps.

## Tooling notes

- Always use MCP doc tools before any web search for OpenAI-related questions.
- If the MCP server is installed but returns no meaningful results, then use web search as a fallback.
- When falling back to web search, restrict to official OpenAI domains (developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com) and cite sources.

PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# M0/M1 Parallel Unblocker Plan

## Summary

Run one coordinated sprint that first cleans the local Git/autostash state, then parallelizes advisor-facing docs, M1 correctness, CI, setup, storage-schema, and LRZ planning work. The gate at the end is explicit: proceed to V0 target-RRI only if M1 is passable; otherwise keep fixing M1 blockers. Do not start stochastic rollout scale or fitted `$Q_H$`.

## Work Packages

- **0. Coordinator: Git/autostash hygiene**
  - Inspect staged, unstaged, untracked, submodule, and `stash@{0}` contents.
  - Separate unrelated rebase/autostash residue from the intended DB/docs changes.
  - Produce a clean staging plan before any subagent writes.
  - Do not drop `stash@{0}` unless its unique contents are confirmed obsolete.

- **1A. Proposal, bibliography, and docs polish**
  - Address proposal freeze, citation hygiene, and doc-alignment polish.
  - Scope: proposal checklist, `docs/references.bib`, roadmap/questions/literature polish where needed.
  - Acceptance: advisor-facing claims use primary citations, no generated/Wikipedia citation slop remains in proposal-critical paths, and touched docs render.

- **1B. M1 contract exploration and candidate-label ordering guards**
  - Map the current offline store, split, frame/CW90, oracle RRI, and candidate-order paths.
  - Add focused tests proving candidate poses, validity masks, depths/points, labels, and serialized payloads stay aligned.
  - Draft the evidence needed for `m1_contract_report.qmd`.

- **1D. Minimal `make ci`, pre-commit, and CI render gate**
  - Add the smallest root-level verification contract that covers agent DB validation, frontmatter checks, and core docs renders.
  - Add pre-commit parity only for already-supported local checks.
  - Avoid broad CI expansion that would block on unavailable datasets or GPUs.

- **2C. `SETUP.md` and one-scene smoke**
  - Write a portable setup guide for environment, CUDA/CPU fallback expectations, dataset/cache paths, and first-run smoke commands.
  - Add one-scene smoke workflow for offline store, Rerun inspector, VIN diagnostics, and docs sanity checks.

- **2E. Zarr/Q/invalidity schema draft only**
  - Draft the rollout/`Q_H` store contract and invalidity taxonomy.
  - Include lineage, target records, candidate tables, validity reason codes, masks, optional heavy diagnostics, and external mesh references.
  - Do not implement large writers or migrate data in this sprint.

- **2F. LRZ dry-run templates and DSS layout**
  - Add dry-run Slurm/Enroot/Pyxis templates for oracle generation, rollout generation, VIN training, and diagnostics.
  - Document DSS staging layout, quota/inode constraints, shard ownership, resume behavior, and atomic-write expectations.
  - Keep templates dry-run/documentary until M1 and storage schema are stable.

## Integration Targets

- Add or update `docs/contents/thesis/m1_contract_report.qmd` with pass/block sections for store, split, frame/CW90, candidate ordering, depth/backprojection, Rerun evidence, throughput, commands, and limitations.
- Integrate candidate-order tests into the package test surface and CI-compatible command list.
- Integrate `SETUP.md`, one-scene smoke docs, minimal CI, bibliography cleanup, and render logs into the M0/M1 evidence path.
- Keep `.agents/*.toml` as the source of truth; GitHub issue mirroring remains secondary.

## Gate

- **Passable M1:** begin V0 GT-OBB target-RRI work.
- **Blocked M1:** continue fixing M1 blockers and record the blocker explicitly in the report and agents DB.
- **Always blocked for now:** stochastic rollout scale, fitted `$Q_H$`, full-scale LRZ generation, Habitat/Isaac, and continuous-policy work.

## Test Plan

- `make agents-db AGENTS_ARGS='validate'`
- `make agents-db`
- `make qmd-frontmatter-check`
- `make check-agent-memory`
- `make ci`
- targeted candidate-order pytest command added by 1B
- `cd docs && quarto render contents/thesis/m1_contract_report.qmd`
- `cd docs && quarto render` for touched proposal-adjacent docs
- CI workflow dry-run by local command parity where possible

## Assumptions

- Subagents get disjoint write scopes and must not touch the Git/autostash cleanup.
- Coordinator reviews and integrates all subagent output before committing.
- The current rebase/autostash state is resolved before parallel file edits begin.
- M1 correctness evidence has priority over new thesis features.

<skill>
<name>mempalace-aria-nbv:code-review-aria-nbv</name>
<path>/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/skills/code-review/SKILL.md</path>
---
name: code-review-aria-nbv
description: Use when reviewing ARIA-NBV changes in the working tree or on a GitHub pull request, especially to produce severity-ranked findings with file and line references for Python, Quarto, Typst, config, and agent-memory changes.
---

# Code Review For ARIA-NBV

## When To Use

Use this skill when the task is to:

- review the current working tree before commit or branch promotion
- review a GitHub pull request diff or requested-review state
- review agent-memory, docs, data-contract, RRI, VIN, or Streamlit changes
- aggregate accepted review feedback into follow-up edits or agents DB records

Do not use this skill for:

- pure implementation without a review ask
- general architecture brainstorming without concrete diffs
- replying to GitHub review threads without also using `github:gh-address-comments` when thread state matters

## Grounding

Before reviewing substantial changes, read:

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. the nearest nested `AGENTS.md` for the touched surface
3. `README.md`
4. `.agents/memory/state/PROJECT_STATE.md`
5. `.agents/AGENTS_INTERNAL_DB.md`

For docs-heavy reviews, also read `docs/AGENTS.md` and start from
`docs/typst/seminar_paper/main.typ`. For package-contract reviews, use
`make context-contracts` before broad source browsing.

## Review Standard

Default to a code-review mindset:

- findings first
- order by severity
- focus on correctness, behavioral regressions, determinism drift, missing validation, repo-boundary leaks, frame/pose mistakes, stale documentation, and operator-facing contract breaks
- include tight file and line references whenever the location is clear
- if there are no findings, say that explicitly and call out residual risk or missing tests
- Prefer tests that exercise public contracts and user-visible behavior. Flag
  tests that only preserve private helper shape when behavior could regress.
- For risky behavior changes, prefer tracer-bullet evidence: one failing
  public-interface behavior test, minimal implementation, repeat.

Use this severity rubric:

- `P0`: data loss, security break, unrecoverable crash, or merge-blocking build or test failure
- `P1`: correctness bug, regression, boundary violation, or broken contract likely to matter immediately
- `P2`: maintainability, observability, or test gap that should be fixed soon
- `P3`: minor polish or documentation issue

## Working Tree Review

1. Establish the review surface with:

```bash
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff
```

2. If the tree is large, narrow by file or subsystem before drawing conclusions.
3. Review tests and docs alongside code changes when contracts moved.
4. Run the narrowest validating commands that can confirm or falsify likely findings.
5. Report findings, then open questions or assumptions, then a brief change summary.

Treat these as first-class review targets in this repo:

- `PoseTW` / `CameraTW` frame consistency and display-only CW90 corrections
- config-as-factory usage through `.setup_target()`
- immutable VIN offline-store and split semantics
- RRI metric meaning, binning semantics, and logged metric names
- VIN candidate-ranking contracts and validation defaults
- docs alignment with `docs/typst/seminar_paper/main.typ`
- agent-memory/debrief hygiene under `.agents/memory/`

## Pull Request Review

1. Resolve the PR from a URL, `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, or the current branch PR.
2. Gather diff and metadata with the lightest tool that works:
   - local git when the branch and base are both present
   - GitHub app, `gh pr view`, or `gh pr diff` when PR context is needed
3. When the task depends on unresolved review threads, inline anchors, or resolution state, use `github:gh-address-comments` instead of guessing from flat comments.
4. Separate new independent findings from existing requested changes and informational comments.
5. Do not submit a review, reply on GitHub, or resolve threads unless the user explicitly asks.

Useful PR commands:

```bash
gh pr view --json number,title,url,baseRefName,headRefName,reviewDecision
gh pr diff
```

## Fan-Out

If the user explicitly asks for delegated or parallel review:

- split review ownership by file area or concern, with disjoint scopes
- keep the aggregation pass local
- do not ask sub-agents to submit reviews or resolve GitHub threads directly

## Output Shape

Use:

1. `Findings`
2. `Open Questions / Assumptions`
3. `Change Summary` or `Residual Risk`

When there are no findings, say:

- no findings identified
- what you validated
- what remains unvalidated

</skill>

- Update RL equations so the finite action is a candidate-table index:
  - `Q_t = {q_{t,i}}_{i=1}^{N_t}`
  - `a_t \in \mathcal{A}(s_t) = {i : m_{t,i}=1}`
  - selected pose/observation uses `q_t = q_{t,a_t}`.

  - Historic raw state: camera streams/calibration/timestamps, trajectory/gravity, semidense points with uncertainty/support, EVL/EFM evidence, detected/predicted OBBs; no GT mesh/GT OBB as actor input.

---

# Create PR

Write PRs that help reviewers understand the change quickly. Keep the body architecture-first: one summary paragraph, explicit verification, a compact work-package overview, then one detailed section per work package.

Use the concrete body pattern in [references/pr-body-shape.md](references/pr-body-shape.md).

## Workflow

1. Ground the branch.
   - Read repo guidance that affects contributor-facing output such as `AGENTS.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any PR template.
   - Inspect `git status -sb`, `git diff --stat`, and the key diffs against the intended base branch.
   - Separate unrelated local edits before staging or publishing.
2. Define the PR shape.
   - Group the branch into 2-7 work packages.
   - Name packages by boundary, contract, or reviewer concern, not by commit order.
   - Prefer scopes such as `API split`, `CLI plumbing`, `adapter cleanup`, `config migration`, `docs refresh`, `benchmark harness`, `UI scaffolding`, or `CI hardening`.
3. Validate before writing.
   - Run the narrowest formatter, linter, and test commands that match the touched surface.
   - Add focused commands when repo-wide validation is too expensive.
   - If a command could not be run, say so explicitly in the PR body.
4. Write the title.
   - Use a concise sentence describing the branch outcome.
   - Prefer product or contract language over implementation trivia.
   - Keep a prefix such as `[codex]` only when another workflow requires it.
5. Write the body using the default shape in [references/pr-body-shape.md](references/pr-body-shape.md).
6. Choose the execution path.
   - If the branch still needs staging, commit, push, or PR creation, pair this skill with the active publish workflow for the session.
   - If the branch is already published, create or update the PR directly with `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit`.

## CLI Execution Path

Prefer explicit GitHub CLI commands over interactive prompts when writing a structured body.

1. Resolve the base branch.
   - If the user names a base branch, use it.
   - Otherwise check `git config branch.$(git branch --show-current).gh-merge-base`.
   - If no branch-specific merge base is configured, use the remote default branch.
2. Write the PR body to a temporary Markdown file.
   - Use `--body-file` so GitHub receives real newlines and tables intact.
   - Treat `--template` as a starting point only. If the repo has a PR template, merge any required prompts into the structured body instead of replacing the work-package format.
3. Create the PR explicitly:

```bash
gh pr create \
  --draft \
  --base "$BASE" \
  --head "$(git branch --show-current)" \
  --title "$TITLE" \
  --body-file "$BODY_FILE"
```

4. Add metadata only when requested or clearly implied:
   - `--reviewer`
   - `--label`
   - `--milestone`
   - `--project`
   - `--assignee`
5. Update an existing PR with the same structured body:

```bash
gh pr edit <number-or-branch> \
  --title "$TITLE" \
  --body-file "$BODY_FILE"
```

## GitHub CLI Notes

- Prefer explicit `--title` and `--body-file` over `gh pr create --fill`.
- Use `gh pr create --draft` by default unless the user explicitly asks for ready review.
- Do not rely on `gh pr create --dry-run` as a no-side-effect probe; it may still push changes.
- Preserve any `--recover <token>` value or generated body file path if creation fails.
- Use `gh pr create --no-maintainer-edit` only when the user explicitly asks for it.
- Use closing keywords such as `Closes #123` only when the branch actually resolves that issue.

## Body Guidance

- Keep `## Summary` to one paragraph that explains the branch at the product and architecture level.
- Under `Focused verification completed:`, list only commands that actually ran.
- Use `## Work Packages` as a compact reviewer map before the detailed sections.
- Use one `## WPn — ...` section per work package.
- Default subsection order inside each work package:
  - `### Scope`
  - `### Key files`
  - `### Initial success criteria resolution`
- Add `### Symbol mapping` when the branch moves public symbols or renames import surfaces.
- Add `### API/path mapping` when the branch moves config fields, file paths, CLI commands, or external contract names.
- Add `### Remaining follow-ups` only when the branch intentionally leaves work unresolved.
- Keep work-package sections outcome-oriented. Do not narrate every commit.

## Status Language

Prefer exact status labels when they fit the evidence:

- `resolved`
- `mostly resolved`
- `partially resolved`
- `not carried forward intentionally`
- `new scope, baseline resolved`
- `new scope, scaffold resolved`

If the status needs nuance, explain it after the label instead of inventing vague wording.

## Review Lens

- If the branch touches core libraries plus adapters or integrations, state whether the boundary stayed clean.
- If the branch touches examples, demos, or app code, clarify whether the change is local to that surface or reflects a broader contract change.
- If the branch touches tooling, docs, or contributor scaffolding, summarize the durable operator or reviewer impact instead of listing files mechanically.
- Mention determinism, rebuildability, deployment, or local-tooling implications when they materially changed.

## Publish Rules

- Reuse the structured body shape instead of GitHub autofill.
- Default to a draft PR unless the user explicitly asks for ready review.
- Never stage unrelated local changes silently.
- Prefer `gh pr edit` over recreating the PR when only the title or body needs revision.

## Output Requirements

- Never paste raw `git diff` into the PR body.
- Never imply validation that did not happen.
- Prefer architecture and contract language over file-by-file changelog prose.
- Keep the body reviewer-first: summary paragraph, verification list, work-package overview, then detailed sections.
- If CLI creation or edit fails, preserve the body file path or recovery token long enough to retry without retyping the body.

</skill>

# Code Review For ARIA-NBV

## When To Use

Use this skill when the task is to:

- review the current working tree before commit or branch promotion
- review a GitHub pull request diff or requested-review state
- review agent-memory, docs, data-contract, RRI, VIN, or Streamlit changes
- aggregate accepted review feedback into follow-up edits or agents DB records

Do not use this skill for:

- pure implementation without a review ask
- general architecture brainstorming without concrete diffs
- replying to GitHub review threads without also using `github:gh-address-comments` when thread state matters

## Grounding

Before reviewing substantial changes, read:

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. the nearest nested `AGENTS.md` for the touched surface
3. `README.md`
4. `.agents/memory/state/PROJECT_STATE.md`
5. `.agents/AGENTS_INTERNAL_DB.md`

For docs-heavy reviews, also read `docs/AGENTS.md` and start from
`docs/typst/seminar_paper/main.typ`. For package-contract reviews, use
`make context-contracts` before broad source browsing.

## Review Standard

Default to a code-review mindset:

- findings first
- order by severity
- focus on correctness, behavioral regressions, determinism drift, missing validation, repo-boundary leaks, frame/pose mistakes, stale documentation, and operator-facing contract breaks
- include tight file and line references whenever the location is clear
- if there are no findings, say that explicitly and call out residual risk or missing tests
- Prefer tests that exercise public contracts and user-visible behavior. Flag
  tests that only preserve private helper shape when behavior could regress.
- For risky behavior changes, prefer tracer-bullet evidence: one failing
  public-interface behavior test, minimal implementation, repeat.

Use this severity rubric:

- `P0`: data loss, security break, unrecoverable crash, or merge-blocking build or test failure
- `P1`: correctness bug, regression, boundary violation, or broken contract likely to matter immediately
- `P2`: maintainability, observability, or test gap that should be fixed soon
- `P3`: minor polish or documentation issue

## Working Tree Review

1. Establish the review surface with:

```bash
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff
```

2. If the tree is large, narrow by file or subsystem before drawing conclusions.
3. Review tests and docs alongside code changes when contracts moved.
4. Run the narrowest validating commands that can confirm or falsify likely findings.
5. Report findings, then open questions or assumptions, then a brief change summary.

Treat these as first-class review targets in this repo:

- `PoseTW` / `CameraTW` frame consistency and display-only CW90 corrections
- config-as-factory usage through `.setup_target()`
- immutable VIN offline-store and split semantics
- RRI metric meaning, binning semantics, and logged metric names
- VIN candidate-ranking contracts and validation defaults
- docs alignment with `docs/typst/seminar_paper/main.typ`
- agent-memory/debrief hygiene under `.agents/memory/`

## Pull Request Review

1. Resolve the PR from a URL, `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, or the current branch PR.
2. Gather diff and metadata with the lightest tool that works:
   - local git when the branch and base are both present
   - GitHub app, `gh pr view`, or `gh pr diff` when PR context is needed
3. When the task depends on unresolved review threads, inline anchors, or resolution state, use `github:gh-address-comments` instead of guessing from flat comments.
4. Separate new independent findings from existing requested changes and informational comments.
5. Do not submit a review, reply on GitHub, or resolve threads unless the user explicitly asks.

Useful PR commands:

```bash
gh pr view --json number,title,url,baseRefName,headRefName,reviewDecision
gh pr diff
```

## Fan-Out

If the user explicitly asks for delegated or parallel review:

- split review ownership by file area or concern, with disjoint scopes
- keep the aggregation pass local
- do not ask sub-agents to submit reviews or resolve GitHub threads directly

## Output Shape

Use:

1. `Findings`
2. `Open Questions / Assumptions`
3. `Change Summary` or `Residual Risk`

When there are no findings, say:

- no findings identified
- what you validated
- what remains unvalidated

</skill>

# Review findings:

## Finding 1 (.agents/skills/aria-nbv-context/scripts/nbv_context_index.sh:72-88) [added]
[P1] Stale source-order still regenerates

The generated context index still emits the seminar paper as fixed ground truth and the old hot-path bundle. Because root guidance routes broad local discovery through this generated source index, `make context` can reintroduce exactly the stale source-order model this PR is meant to remove. Update this generator, and the checked-in context map, to point at `.agents/references/source_order.md` and the role-split substrate/current-direction/proposal sources.

## Finding 2 (.agents/skills/aria-nbv-context/SKILL.md:13-18) [added]
[P2] Do not hard-require ignored generated context

`docs/_generated/context/source_index.md` is ignored output, but the new metadata lists it as `must_read`. A fresh checkout or clean workspace will not have it, so routers may fail or do unnecessary generation before even using this discovery skill. Keep generated context in the workflow as optional or generated-on-demand, not in the hard `must_read` set.

## Finding 3 (.agents/skills/semantic-scholar-litkg/SKILL.md:72-77) [added]
[P2] KG toolkit validation lost its working directory

The skill now tells agents to run `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo test` without saying to run them inside `.agents/external/litkg-rs` or using `--manifest-path`. There is no Cargo workspace at the ARIA-NBV repo root, so a normal agent following this from root will fail. Mirror the metadata command style or explicitly prefix the submodule working directory.

## Finding 4 (.agents/skills/docs-curator/SKILL.md:3-10) [added]
[P2] Docs skill still owns too much internal agent surface

`docs-curator` applies to canonical memory and all `.agents/references/**`, while `agents-db`, `aria-litkg-memory`, and `agent-behavior` also own parts of that same internal scaffold surface. This keeps broad routing ambiguous: an internal reference or memory-only change can still load the docs workflow even when no public-doc boundary is involved. # Plan Grill

## When To Use

Use this skill before implementing ambiguous or high-impact work:

- thesis scope, advisor-facing claims, or roadmap changes
- entity-aware RRI, target-conditioned VIN, rollout/RL, or simulator choices
- docs/public-internal partitioning, scaffold changes, or KG architecture
- broad cleanup where ownership, compatibility, or evidence bar is unclear

Do not use it for an already-localized bug with a concrete failing command; use
`diagnose-aria` instead.

## Grounding

Before asking the user, answer discoverable questions from:

1. `.agents/references/source_order.md`
2. `docs/typst/seminar_paper/main.typ` for implemented substrate claims
3. `.agents/memory/state/PROJECT_STATE.md`
4. `.agents/memory/state/DECISIONS.md`
5. `.agents/memory/state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`
6. `docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ`
7. `docs/contents/thesis/roadmap.qmd`
8. `docs/contents/thesis/questions.qmd`
9. the nearest `AGENTS.md` for touched code or docs

Use `aria-nbv-context` if the relevant surface is not yet localized.

## Interview Rules

- Ask one material decision at a time.
- State the recommended answer with the tradeoff.
- Challenge overloaded terms against `docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ`.
- For fuzzy thesis or planning terms, test the plan with three concrete
  scenarios: one normal case, one boundary case, and one failure case.
- Cross-check claims against code, paper, memory state, and roadmap before
  accepting them.
- Resolved terminology updates `docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ` or
  `.agents/memory/state/DECISIONS.md`. Do not add a parallel root context file
  or ADR tree as a second source of truth.
- Distinguish `current`, `planned`, `scratch`, and `archive` docs.
- Capture durable outcomes in the smallest correct surface:
  - invariant -> `AGENTS.md`
  - workflow -> `.agents/skills/`
  - current truth -> `.agents/memory/state/`
  - backlog -> `.agents/*.toml`
  - public narrative -> `docs/` or Typst
  - human preference -> `.agents/references/human_owner_intent.md`

## Output

End with a decision-complete plan that names:

- goal and success criteria
- in/out of scope
- public interfaces or docs surfaces affected
- implementation packages
- verification commands
- assumptions and deferred decisions

</skill>

# Simplification

Use this skill for behavior-preserving pruning of the current intended surface.
Use `agent-behavior` for general simplicity/surgical-change principles on
ordinary work.

## Modes

- Default simplification: reduce redundancy, stale surface, and unnecessary
  indirection while preserving intended behavior.
- Ruthless simplification: only when explicitly requested. Read
  `references/ruthless.md` before planning or editing.

## Workflow

1. Establish the current contract and baseline verification.
2. Use focused `rg`, narrow reads, and `references/redundancy-discovery.md` to
   find actual overlap or dead surface.
3. Choose the smallest behavior-preserving cut.
4. Prefer deleting, merging, or inlining over adding new abstraction.
5. Validate with focused tests and formatting/lint checks for the touched
   surface.
6. Record backlog changes only when the cleanup materially changes active debt.

## Rules

- Prefer deletion over abstraction.
- Prefer inlining over helper extraction for single-use or forwarding helpers.
- Keep one canonical owner per semantic concept.
- Do not widen APIs or add compatibility scaffolding unless explicitly asked.
- Do not preserve stale wrappers, deprecated import paths, or no-op config
  flags unless they are active public contracts named by the task.
- Move genuinely shared behavior to the canonical shared owner instead of
  leaving quasi-shared helpers in leaf modules.
- Treat analyzer output as advisory; repo ownership and tests decide.

## Tooling

- Use `rg` first for local checks.
- Use code-index or analyzer tools only after the candidate surface is broader
  than a quick local search.
- See `references/tool-decision-tree.md` for the optional analyzer workflow.

## Verification

- Focused tests for the changed surface.
- `ruff format <file>` and `ruff check <file>` for Python changes.
- `make loc` before and after when LOC reduction is part of the decision.
- `make ci` before commit when the change is broad.

</skill>

- docs/public-internal partitioning, scaffold changes, or KG architecture

# RQ1 Objective Reformulation

## Summary
Replace the current `J_e = sum RRI_e(...)` formulation with a split contract:

- `J_e` becomes an endpoint target-quality gain under a fixed view budget.
- `G_t^(H)` remains the finite-horizon cumulative target-RRI return for rollout and `Q_H` training.
- A log-error gain is documented as a scale/stage-stability companion formulation, with exact adoption left as an explicit open decision.

This fixes the feasibility issue: the old `J_e` sums state-relative ratios, so it is horizon-dependent and not interpretable as a bounded reconstruction-quality score.

## Proposed RQ1 Text
In [questions.qmd](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/docs/contents/thesis/questions.qmd), replace the concrete formulation with this structure:

```tex
For a rollout rooted at state s_0, target e, horizon H, and valid action
sequence tau=(a_0,...,a_{H-1}), let q_t=q_{t,a_t} and
P_{t+1}=P_t \cup P_{q_t}. Define the target-cropped distance

D_e(P) = d(C_e(P), M_e),

where C_e filters reconstructed points to the matched target crop and M_e is
the GT target surface used only for oracle supervision and evaluation.

The primary equal-budget trajectory metric is endpoint target-quality gain:

J_{e,\Delta}^{(H)}(\tau)
=
\frac{D_e(P_0)-D_e(P_H)}{D_e(P_0)+\varepsilon}.
```

Then define, separately:

```tex
r_t^e
=
\mathrm{RRI}_e(q_t \mid P_t, M_e)
=
\frac{D_e(P_t)-D_e(P_{t+1})}{D_e(P_t)+\varepsilon},
\qquad
G_0^{(H)}(\tau)
=
\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^t r_t^e.
```

And include the log companion as an open ablation:

```tex
L_e^{(H)}(\tau)
=
\log(D_e(P_0)+\varepsilon)-\log(D_e(P_H)+\varepsilon)
=
\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}
\left[
\log(D_e(P_t)+\varepsilon)-\log(D_e(P_{t+1})+\varepsilon)
\right].
```

## Pros And Cons
Endpoint gain `J_{e,\Delta}^{(H)}`:
- Pros: directly answers “how much target error was removed after H views”; comparable under equal budget; bounded above by 1 when reconstruction distance does not worsen.
- Cons: not additive, so it is less convenient for bootstrapped `Q_H` targets; can hide whether a method improves early or only at the last view.
- Mitigation: report quality-vs-view curves or AUC alongside the endpoint value.

Cumulative return `G_0^(H)`:
- Pros: matches the existing glossary and `Q_H` rollout/value-learning notation; works with masked finite-horizon value targets.
- Cons: not a normalized quality score; sums ratios with changing denominators; should not be named `J_e`.
- Decision: keep it for training and rollout ranking, not as the main RQ1 trajectory metric.

Log gain `L_e^(H)`:
- Pros: telescopes cleanly, is additive across steps, and may handle stage-dependent distance scales better.
- Cons: not bounded to `[0,1]`, depends on epsilon near near-solved targets, and is less directly tied to VIN-NBV’s RRI convention.
- Decision: include it as a planned comparison/ablation, with exact epsilon, clipping, and adoption criteria left open.

## Implementation Changes
- Update only RQ1 in [questions.qmd](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/docs/contents/thesis/questions.qmd) unless a consistency check reveals direct contradictions elsewhere.
- If adding a named glossary term for endpoint gain, update [glossary.typ](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/docs/typst/shared/glossary.typ); otherwise reuse existing `target-specific-rri`, `target-rri-reward`, and `finite-horizon-return`.
- Record the unresolved details in [OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](/home/jd/repos/ARIA-NBV/.agents/memory/state/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md): gamma default, epsilon/clipping policy, whether log gain becomes a reported primary companion metric, and target eligibility when `D_e(P_0)` is near zero.

## Stress Tests
Normal case: two policies use the same `H`; the one with lower final target distance gets higher `J_{e,\Delta}^{(H)}`.

Boundary case: different budgets are not compared by raw `J` alone; use fixed-budget tables or quality-cost/AUC curves.

Failure case: a valid action worsens target distance, yielding negative immediate reward or endpoint gain. Invalid candidates remain masked and are not encoded as low RRI.

## Verification
- `make qmd-frontmatter-check`
- `cd docs && quarto render contents/thesis/questions.qmd`
- `make kg-claim-check KG_CLAIM="RQ1 separates endpoint target-quality gain J_e from finite-horizon cumulative target-RRI return G_H for Q_H training and treats log target-error gain as an open ablation"`

- Update `docs/literature/README.md` to list DQN and its local source tree.

## Literature Distillation
Add a dedicated `Q_H and DQN` section to `docs/contents/literature/rl_planning.qmd`.

Ground the section in:
- DQN 2013 source files:
  - `intro.tex`: delayed rewards, correlated samples, non-stationary behavior distribution, experience replay.
  - `background.tex`: discounted return, Bellman/Q-learning objective, off-policy greedy value learning.
  - `method.tex`: replay tuples, random minibatches, data-efficiency, decorrelation, one output per valid action.
  - `experiments.tex`: held-out predicted-Q tracking and reward/scale clipping as stability context, not ARIA defaults.
- Double DQN source:
  - target network and replay as DQN stabilizers;
  - max-over-action overestimation;
  - online network selects the greedy action while target network evaluates it;
  - overestimation risk grows with noisy value estimates over action sets.
- IQL source:
  - offline RL must avoid querying unseen/out-of-distribution actions;
  - SARSA-style in-sample backup;
  - expectile value fitting as an upper in-support value approximation;
  - Q backup through `V(s')`;
  - advantage-weighted policy extraction as later bridge work, not first-path thesis success.

## ARIA-NBV Adoption
Update the `rl.qh` glossary entry and the new `rl_planning.qmd` section to state:
- `Q_H` is a candidate-query Transformer over a finite masked candidate table.
- DQN contributes replayed transition learning, Bellman-style TD targets, and batched per-candidate value scoring.
- Double DQN contributes the default masked selector/evaluator backup for reducing finite-candidate overestimation.
- IQL contributes the offline support discipline: do not query or optimize over unavailable/unlogged actions; treat IQL-style expectile/value losses as a gated ablation after `Q_H`.
- Invalid actions remain hard-masked, not low-reward actions.
- Atari CNN architecture, Atari hyperparameters, epsilon-greedy exploration, and reward clipping are not adopted as ARIA defaults.
